title: The Map Is Not the Territory
coreMove: Test a representation against ground truth before letting it govern the decision.
sourcePressure: The source says maps, models, financial statements, policy documents, manuals, resumes, and performance reviews are reductions of reality. It anchors the idea in Bezos testing a customer-service metric, Newton and Einstein showing useful but incomplete maps, and Jane Jacobs warning against forcing living cities into abstract plans.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says data is inferior to anecdotes or that all maps should be distrusted.

sourceAnchors.name: Jeff Bezos
sourceAnchors.detail: customer complaint anecdotes conflicted with Amazon's reported call-wait metric, and a live phone call showed the metric was missing the territory
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A dashboard said the line was moving; Bezos picked up the phone and let the customer line answer back.

sourceAnchors.name: Jane Jacobs
sourceAnchors.detail: her city-planning critique is used to show how people try to force living cities to fit abstract plans
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Jane Jacobs matters because the plan did not merely describe the city; it tried to make the city obey the drawing.

sourceAnchors.name: Newton and Einstein
sourceAnchors.detail: Newtonian physics remains useful while Einstein's special relativity shows that an older map can be incomplete in some domains
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Newton's map still gets you across much of the terrain, but Einstein showed where the terrain changed under its feet.

hook: spreadsheet bad because human story good

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: an operations lead whose call-center report shows healthy wait times
exampleSpecs.stakes: renewal calls are being lost while the executive team trusts a green metric
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire calls the support line from the conference room speakerphone and lets the actual hold music run past the dashboard's promised answer time
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tinny hold music filling a glass conference room

exampleSpecs.audience: a conservation coordinator reading a neat habitat map
exampleSpecs.stakes: grant money may be spent on the wrong bend of the river
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael places the laminated habitat map beside muddy boot photos from the riverbank and delays the grant order until the two disagreeing pictures are reconciled
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet boot prints drying on the tailgate beside a laminated river map

exampleSpecs.audience: a plant manager selecting candidates from polished resumes
exampleSpecs.stakes: the wrong hire will slow a short-staffed apprenticeship bench
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel compares a perfect resume with a five-minute bench test and watches the weaker paper candidate solve the caliper setup cleanly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a digital caliper blinking beside two printed resumes

exampleSpecs.audience: a parks planner relying on a clean safety diagram
exampleSpecs.stakes: children may avoid the new layout because the plan misses how families actually move
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Olivier follow parents across the site with a clipboard and mark the desire paths that never appear on the approved plan
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chalk arrows crossing the mulch before the new swings arrive

exampleSpecs.audience: a market treasurer trusting a clean vendor-revenue sheet
exampleSpecs.stakes: a fee increase could drive out the small vendors who make the market worth visiting
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aman counts the empty end stalls at closing and writes the missing vendors directly onto the revenue sheet before approving the fee change
exampleSpecs.firstImage: folded stall weights lined up where two vegetable tents used to stand

exampleSpecs.audience: a reliability lead whose uptime report excludes degraded login failures
exampleSpecs.stakes: customers are technically online while unable to complete work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marit reads one customer screen recording beside the uptime incident log and changes the incident definition before the weekly report goes out
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frozen login spinner on a customer's screen recording

skillTargets: identify when a proxy has outrun ground truth
choose a reality check for a representation
notice when a map starts changing behavior

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one trusted report or plan. Write one concrete territory check you can do before the next decision that depends on it.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
